//: pi config for the Stage 2 review pass (BiggiePockets/.github).
pi resolves models from the config dir pointed at by PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR. This file
declares the OpenRouter provider and every model Stage 2 is allowed to run on, each
with its OpenRouter list rates, so a FRESH CI runner (no cached models-store.json)
resolves them deterministically. These models are absent from the catalog pi ships
and the live catalog refresh is a background fetch, not a startup step we can rely
on.
This is the allowlist behind the workflow.s pi_model input. A repo may point itself
at any id listed here; the workflow fails early, by name, on a slug that is not.
The default when a caller says nothing is deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash.
Context: the DeepSeek models carry ~1M tokens, Claude Haiku 4.5 carries 200k. Stage 2
reads a diff plus the Codex handoff, so a very large pull request has less headroom on
Haiku than the numbers elsewhere in this file suggest.
Rates are $/1M tokens exactly as OpenRouter publishes them at the time of pinning.
pi computes cost.total from these, so they are what OpenRouter bills for standard
usage and what Datadog attributes spend from. Adding a model means adding its id
AND its published rates together; rolling one means updating both.
The apiKey interpolation reads OPENROUTER_API_KEY from the workflow environment
(the same org secret the Codex stage uses) — no interactive login or OAuth is
involved. api/api identify the OpenAI-compatible endpoint pi uses.
